title: Woodall’s conjecture
formal: For every finite weakly connected loopless directed multigraph \(D\) that is not strongly connected, let \(\tau(D)\) be the minimum size of a directed cut. Do there exist \(\tau(D)\) pairwise arc-disjoint dijoins in \(D\)? All arcs have unit capacity, and a dijoin must meet every directed cut.
definitions:
A directed multigraph is a finite vertex set \(V\), a finite set \(A\) of individually distinguished arcs, and two maps \(\operatorname{tail},\operatorname{head}:A\to V\). For every arc its tail differs from its head. Parallel arcs and arcs in both directions between the same vertices are allowed. Weak connectivity means that every two vertices are connected after forgetting arc directions. Strong connectivity means that every ordered pair of vertices is joined by a directed path, including a path of length zero from a vertex to itself. The graph is assumed weakly connected and not strongly connected, so in particular it has at least two vertices.

For \(\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V\), define
\[
\delta^+(U)=\{a\in A:\operatorname{tail}(a)\in U,\ \operatorname{head}(a)\notin U\},
\qquad
\delta^-(U)=\{a\in A:\operatorname{tail}(a)\notin U,\ \operatorname{head}(a)\in U\}.
\]
A directed cut, also called a dicut, is \(\delta^+(U)\) for such a set \(U\) with \(\delta^-(U)=\varnothing\). The hypotheses ensure that the family of dicuts is nonempty and none of its members is empty. Thus
\[
\tau(D)=\min\{|\delta^+(U)|:\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V,\ \delta^-(U)=\varnothing\}
\]
is a well-defined positive integer. Parallel arcs are counted separately.

A dijoin is a subset \(J\subseteq A\) such that \(J\cap B\ne\varnothing\) for every dicut \(B\). A family \(J_1,\ldots,J_{\tau(D)}\) is pairwise arc-disjoint when \(J_i\cap J_j=\varnothing\) for all \(i\ne j\). It need not cover all arcs. No arc has a weight, capacity zero or capacity greater than one. This is an existence assertion, without an algorithm, running-time bound, randomness, approximation or restricted graph class.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof that every graph in the stated domain has \(\tau(D)\) pairwise arc-disjoint dijoins, or exhibit a finite graph in that domain and give a complete Lean proof that no such family exists. The target is the universal min–max assertion; it is not a numerical approximation to a packing value. A constant-fraction guarantee, a fractional packing, a theorem for a proper subclass or a counterexample requiring zero-capacity arcs does not settle it.

context_blocks.text: Each dijoin intercepts every one-way boundary of a digraph. Disjoint dijoins provide separate complete covers without sharing any arc; the smallest boundary bounds the number of such covers. The conjecture asserts that this bound is always attainable.
Schrijver’s Survey Question 34 is the structural equality specified here. The adjacent Question 33 concerns finding a maximum packing in polynomial time, which is a separate algorithmic target.

The weighted Edmonds–Giles generalization is false. Its zero-capacity arcs still affect which vertex partitions are dicuts, so simply deleting those arcs does not give a counterexample to the unit-capacity conjecture.

The 2025 Combinatorica paper proves a polynomial-time guarantee of \(\lfloor\tau/6\rfloor\) disjoint dijoins. This resolves the older question of whether three disjoint dijoins are guaranteed when the minimum dicut size is sufficiently large, while leaving the exact equality open.

The May 2026 revision of the chordal-digraph paper proves the weighted equality when the underlying undirected graph is chordal, meaning it has no induced cycle of length at least four. This restricted theorem does not establish the general unweighted conjecture.

The graph hypotheses select the nontrivial cut-packing case. A weakly disconnected graph has an empty cut under this convention; a strongly connected graph has no dicuts. Excluding these degeneracies avoids assigning artificial minimum or packing values.

why: Woodall’s conjecture asks whether the visible cut bottleneck completely determines the supply of disjoint directed-cut covers. It is a basic integral packing–covering question in combinatorial optimization, with exact structure beyond known approximation guarantees.

importance.reason: A longstanding min–max conjecture in combinatorial optimization, singled out in Schrijver’s survey and the focus of recent approximation and integrality research. The direct packing/covering and algorithmic connections justify inclusion within optimization.

sentences: A dicut is a nonempty one-way boundary in a directed graph, and a dijoin is a set of arcs meeting every dicut.
The smallest dicut bounds how many pairwise disjoint dijoins can exist.
Woodall’s conjecture states that this bound is always attained in the unweighted setting.
The card allows parallel arcs, fixes the nontrivial connectivity regime and keeps the statement separate from the false weighted generalization.
A proof or counterexample would settle a longstanding integral packing–covering equality beyond known constant-factor and graph-class results.
